evidence.original_text: The University of Minnesota Medical School offers seven dual-degree programs for a degree in medical research (MD/PhD), public health (MD/MPH), biomedical engineering (MD/MS), law (MD/JD), business (MD/MBA), or health informatics (MD/MHI).[15]
The University of Minnesota Medical School is a medical school at the University of Minnesota. It is a combination of three campuses located in Minneapolis, Duluth, and St. Cloud, Minnesota.
Type: Public

[edit | edit source]
The University of Minnesota Medical School began in 1888 when three of the private medical schools in the Twin Cities in Minnesota merged their programs to form the University of Minnesota Medical School.[3] A fourth school was integrated in 1908. As a consequence of these mergers, the school is one of two in the state, the other being the Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine in Rochester, Minnesota.[4] The University of Minnesota Medical School's older buildings include the Mayo Memorial Building (1954) and Jackson Hall (1912). Jackson Hall was built as the home of the Institute of Anatomy and is still the site of anatomy instruction for students.[5]

[edit | edit source]
The University of Minnesota Medical School is part of the Academic Health Centers (AHC) in the United States. The AHC comprises the Medical School, School of Dentistry, School of Nursing, College of Pharmacy, School of Public Health, and the College of Veterinary Medicine.[14]
The University of Minnesota Medical School offers seven dual-degree programs for a degree in medical research (MD/PhD), public health (MD/MPH), biomedical engineering (MD/MS), law (MD/JD), business (MD/MBA), or health informatics (MD/MHI).[15] The Medical School also offers 10 pathways for students to experience longitudinal integrated clerkships at hosting sites, each with a different focus.[16] A longitudinal integrated clerkship was implemented at the University of Minnesota Medical School in 1971. Jack Verby created the Rural Physicians Associate Program (RPAP) as a workforce initiative for rural Minnesota.[17]
Duluth is also a primary site for the Center for American Indian and Minority Health.[19][better source needed]

[edit | edit source]
The University of Minnesota Medical School has partnered with Fairview Health Services in 1997, making the university hospital under Fairview operations and eventually moving pediatrics to the West Bank, and with its group practice, University of Minnesota Physicians, also known as M Physicians, is the multispecialty group practice composed of faculty from the University of Minnesota Medical School.
A partnership between the University of Minnesota Physicians and Fairview Health Services was formalized through a 2019 agreement. The partnership included 11 hospitals and 56 primary care clinics, which were managed by Fairview.[26]

value.text:
The University of Minnesota Medical School is a public medical school within the University of Minnesota in Minnesota, United States. Its activities span locations in Minneapolis, Duluth and St. Cloud. It teaches medicine and participates in the university’s wider health sciences environment, alongside schools and colleges covering dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, public health and veterinary medicine. The school’s organizational position is distinct from that of its parent university.

The medical school began in 1888 through the merger of programs from three private medical schools in the Twin Cities. A fourth school was integrated in 1908. Its older teaching buildings include Jackson Hall, built in 1912 as the home of the Institute of Anatomy, and the Mayo Memorial Building, dating from 1954. The school’s history also includes the Rural Physicians Associate Program, created in 1971 as a workforce initiative for rural Minnesota.

Its academic provision includes dual-degree combinations linking medicine with research, public health, biomedical engineering, law, business and health informatics. Longitudinal integrated clerkships provide different pathways for clinical experience. The Duluth campus has a role in the Center for American Indian and Minority Health. The medical school also works with Fairview Health Services and University of Minnesota Physicians in clinical partnerships.
